2021.headline: Inspection volume returns to pre-pandemic levels.
2021.note: 2021 recorded 2,940 Class A/B dog and cat inspections, with Missouri accounting for roughly a third of all inspections in our dataset. Records-access violations were the most frequently cited issue, consistent with every other year in this audit.

2022.headline: The highest inspection volume in this five-year dataset.
2022.note: At 3,562 inspections, 2022 saw more Class A/B dog and cat inspections than any other completed year on file. The violation rate ticked up to 13.1%, with records-access and veterinary care issues the most common citations.

2023.headline: Nearly 1 in 5 inspections found problems, the highest violation rate on record.
2023.note: 2023’s 19.2% violation rate is the peak in our dataset, and critical NCIs reached 35, also a high. Records-access and veterinary care violations were the most frequently cited issues.

2024.headline: Violation rates ease from the 2023 peak, but records-access issues persist.
2024.note: After 2023’s high, the violation rate dropped to 14.4% and critical NCIs fell from 35 to 7. Records-access remained the most-cited violation category, with veterinary care close behind.

2025.headline: Inspection volume dips, but critical violations climb back up.
2025.note: 2025 recorded 2,704 Class A/B dog and cat inspections, fewer than 2022, 2023, or 2024, while critical NCIs rose to 17. Records-access violations remained the top-cited issue. Part of the dip in inspection volume is tied to the federal government shutdown from October 1 to November 12, 2025, during which routine APHIS Animal Welfare Act inspections were suspended.

2026.headline: Year in progress, data through September.
2026.note: 2026 is still in progress. Through September, 2,090 inspections have been logged with a 15.0% violation rate. USDA posts inspection reports with a delay of about four weeks, so the most recent weeks may still be undercounted. Treat this tab as a partial snapshot, not a year-end total.
